verdict.rationale: Figma Make's docs show it generates frontend apps from prompts, and its own feature lets you add a backend to store and manage data. The documented flow is sequential, though: you generate the frontend, then create a backend. Nothing shows one prompt producing both UI and backend logic, and the backend is described only as data storage and management. Missing for 10: evidence of single-prompt full-stack generation, documentation of backend business logic beyond storing data, independent or hands-on corroboration of backend generation.

support.subject: As a developer, I can generate both frontend UI and backend logic from a single prompt

citations.quote: Generate and design your frontend in Figma Make, then create a backend to manage your content.
You can also [add a backend](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/32640822050199) to your app to securely store and manage data.
Figma Make's AI writes React code rather than creating a Figma drawing.
